subject: Unexpected rate-limit failures impacting Halcyon: request for remediation and evidence
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@halcyon.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected 429s hitting production — need root cause and ETA

Hi Sean,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 429 rate-limit responses this morning across our production API keys (multiple services). Attached is a short export of metrics from 08:00–09:00 PT with sample request IDs (first column). Impact: our ingestion pipelines are dropping data and our ML job queue is backing up.

Can you confirm whether this is a customer-side surge or something on Redwood's quota side? We saw token usage that looks within our expected envelope. We need:
- Immediate mitigation options (workarounds we can apply)
- A short explanation of root cause or what you are investigating
- Customer-facing evidence for our internal audit (request IDs and server-side error traces)

We have an internal exec meeting at 11:30 PT and would appreciate a quick note before then.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Halcyon AI

Attachment: halcyon_metric_export.csv (CSV, 78KB)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@halcyon.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s hitting production — need root cause and ETA

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads up and the export. Sorry for the disruption.

Short update: we see a spike of 429s correlated with your tenant IDs that looks like an incorrect routing to a lower-capacity quota pool. Our infra team has temporarily exempted your tenant from the burst aggregation to reduce throttling; you should see immediate improvement in the next 3–5 minutes.

Can you confirm one or two of the request IDs from your export (we pulled a few but want to match exactly)? If you can share any request IDs that hit between 08:05–08:20 PT, that will help our postmortem trace.

We will follow up with a short remediation summary and proposed credit for the dropped requests. If agreeable, I'd like to schedule a 30‑minute post-incident sync Monday to walk through the fix and the preventive changes. Proposed times: Mon 10:00 or 14:00 PT.

Quick contact details: Sean Gallagher, Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference — +1 415-555-0126

—Sean

Subject: Internal: Halcyon 429s — quick RCA and credit calc

Team —

Summary of what I have so far:
- Symptom: sustained 429s for Halcyon tenant across multiple API keys starting ~08:02 PT on 2025-07-12.
- Immediate mitigation applied: exempted from burst aggregation (temporary policy override) at 08:50 PT — error rate decreased noticeably.

Preliminary root cause (Karthik please correct/add): during a recent routing config rollout (2025-07-11 midnight UTC) an edge case in the mapping script caused tenant namespace hashes ending in 0x3 to be assigned to quota-pool B instead of quota-pool A. Quota-pool B has a stricter token window threshold; Halcyon's tenants landed in pool B.

Karthik, recommended remediation and timeline? Also need an estimate of number of failed requests we should credit Halcyon for (safe approach: all 429s in the 08:00–09:00 window while mapping was incorrect). Grace, can you draft a one-paragraph postmortem blurb for the customer?

Thanks — will compile and send customer-facing note once we have precise counts.

—Sean

Subject: Post-incident summary and remediation confirmation — Halcyon AI

Hi Maya,

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated. This note summarizes what happened, what we changed, and the next steps (including credits and evidence links).

What happened
- Between 08:02–08:58 PT on 2025-07-12, several Halcyon tenant IDs were incorrectly assigned to a lower-capacity quota pool due to an edge-case in a routing-table rollout (mapping script bug introduced 2025-07-11). This caused higher-than-expected 429 responses for requests that were otherwise within Halcyon's contractual token envelope.

What we changed (remediation)
- Immediate: temporary policy override to bypass burst aggregation for affected tenant IDs (applied 08:50 PT on 2025-07-12) — eliminated the immediate throttle.
- Permanent: corrected the mapping script and pushed a targeted config rollback + validation tests to prevent hash-edge-case misassignment. Deployed 2025-07-13 02:40 PT.
- Preventive: added an automated canary that verifies tenant->quota-pool mappings for newly rolled configs, and an alert rule when a tenant's 429 rate exceeds a 0.5% threshold for 10 minutes.

Customer impact and credits
- We count 12,320 requests from Halcyon that returned 429s during the impacted window. We propose a one-time credit equivalent to the billed token cost for those requests (see attached calculation). We additionally offer a goodwill 10% service credit for the impacted hour.

Evidence and artifacts
- Attached: redwood_quota_map.json (mapping snapshot showing pre-fix assignment), halcyon_metric_export.csv (customer-provided sample), signed_credit_agreement.pdf (finalized agreement for the credit).
- Internal ticket: https://support.redwood.com/tickets/RED-78934
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-halcyon-remediation (postmortem doc, timeline, validation logs).

Next steps
- Please confirm the attached credit agreement and preferred billing contact and we will apply the credit to your account by the end of July billing cycle.
- If you'd like a walkthrough of the postmortem and our new guardrails, Karthik and I are available Mon 10:00 PT.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a high-priority postmortem and have already implemented safeguards to prevent recurrence.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
Sean: +1 415-555-0126
